guide: Open Start and type your imprint name, the title of your next launch and your own targets in the yellow cells: reviews per copy, open rate, cost per subscriber, payback of a swap and the list size you want.
Check Titles, Team and Launch Steps. Titles holds the release dates and pre-orders, Team holds the phones for the message links and Launch Steps holds the standard days from release.

Write each launch step in Launch Tasks with its owner, due date and done date. The step check, days late and the later steps waiting fill in by themselves; Launch Readiness and Late Launch Steps show what to do first.
Keep the reviewer list in Reviewers and write every advance copy in Advance Copies. The overdue check, reviews per 100 copies, Reviewer Ranking and Response by Title fill in.
Write each newsletter send in Newsletter Sends, then the new and lost subscribers by source in Subscribers by Source. List Growth by Month, Send Results and Cost per Subscriber by Source fill in.
Write each swap and paid promotion in Swaps and Promotions. Swap Results works out the cost per subscriber, the payback and a swap again verdict with the numbers on Start (your own numbers).
After a launch write the copies of the first 7 and 30 days in Launch Results. The launch share and the verdict against your own average fill in; the pre-order columns feed the momentum check.
Use the 18 calculators to judge the launch, rank the late steps, plan the reviews, test the list, forecast its growth and check the pre-order pace.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.

A first-time author with one to three books keeps one launch, a short reviewer list and one send a month; a small press reads the pen-name columns as author columns. Figures are estimates until the stores pay.

listing.title: Author and Self-Publisher Readers, Newsletter and Launch Planner Excel Template: Launch Plan, Reviewer List, List Growth, Swap Payback
listing.headline: Launch every book with a plan, a reviewer list and a newsletter you can measure
listing.description:
Run the reader side of an author or small publishing business in one Excel workbook. Built for an independent author who publishes under one or two pen names, often with a part-time assistant and a launch coordinator. Launch Tasks lists every launch step with its owner, due date, days late and a step check, and Launch Readiness turns the next launch into a ready, at risk or delay verdict. Late Launch Steps ranks the open steps by days late and by the later steps that wait on them.

Reviewers and Advance Copies keep the reviewer list (an advance copy is a free copy sent to a reviewer before release): copies sent, review due, review posted, response rate, reviews per 100 copies sent and a keep, test or remove verdict for each reviewer. Newsletter Sends, Subscribers by Source and List Growth by Month show the list size, new and lost readers, open and click rates, cost per subscriber and royalties per 1,000 readers. Swap Results works out the payback of each swap or paid promotion against your own numbers. Launch Results sets the first 7 and 30 days against your own average launch share, and the pre-order check compares your pre-orders with your last two launches.

18 calculators cover the launch verdict, the late steps, launch share, review targets, reminders, reviewer ranking, list growth in three scenarios, cost per subscriber, swap payback, partners, clean-up and the launch week plan. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to reviewers, swap partners, an assistant, a launch coordinator and the author.

This is part five of the Author and Self-Publisher Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Figures are estimates until the stores pay, and every target is your own number. It helps you keep track and does not promise sales.

documents.title: Reviewer invitation letter
paragraphs: Letter of {set:company}, dated {today}. Dear {col:reviewers.name}, thank you for being on our reviewer list since {col:reviewers.joined_on}.

We would like to invite you to read the next book before it is released. An advance copy is a free copy sent to a reviewer before release. There is no duty to write a review and no duty to praise the book. An honest review, a short one, helps other readers.
If you would like a copy, reply to this letter and tell us your preferred format. We will write the due date for the review on the cover note.
Thank you for your time.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own business.

documents.title: Advance copy cover note
paragraphs: Cover note of {set:company}, dated {today}. Dear {col:arcs.reviewer}, here is your advance copy of {col:arcs.title}, sent on {col:arcs.sent_on}.
Please read it at your own pace. If you would like to post a review, the date we hope for is {col:arcs.due_on}. A review is welcome but never a duty. Please do not share the file.
Say in your review that you received a free advance copy. Check each store's current terms for how to post it.
With thanks for your help.

documents.title: Review reminder letter
paragraphs: Letter of {set:company}, dated {today}. Dear {col:arcs.reviewer}, a friendly reminder about {col:arcs.title}.
The copy was sent on {col:arcs.sent_on}, which is {col:arcs.days_since_sent} days ago, and the review was hoped for by {col:arcs.due_on}. The copy check says: {col:arcs.check}.
If you have no time, that is fine. Please tell us so that we can keep your place on the list for the next book. If the review is ready, thank you.
With kind regards.

Morning. Check that the book is live on every store page and that the price is the launch price set by {col:titles.price_on}. Send the launch day newsletter. Post the launch message on your own channels.
Afternoon. Answer reader messages. Note the first copies sold. Ask the assistant to check the store pages ({col:titles.va_name}).

Plan the pushes of the launch week: the teaser was due on {col:titles.teaser_on}; one send on the day before release; the launch day send on {col:titles.release_date}; one reminder send two or three days after. Your own limit is on the Start sheet and the Launch Week Plan sheet checks it.

paragraphs: Swap result report of {set:company}, dated {today}. Partner: {col:swapres.partner}. Date: {col:swapres.date}. Kind: {col:swapres.kind}.

Cost: {col:swapres.cost}. Subscribers gained: {col:swapres.subscribers}. Cost per subscriber: {col:swapres.cost_per_sub}. Sales in 7 days: {col:swapres.sales_7d}. Royalties in 7 days: {col:swapres.royalties}. Value of the readers gained: {col:swapres.value}.
Payback: {col:swapres.payback} (1.00 means paid back). Verdict: {col:swapres.verdict}. This partner has {col:swapres.partner_swaps} swaps with an average of {col:swapres.partner_avg} readers.
Figures are estimates, the values per copy and per reader are your own numbers.

documents.title: Launch result report with your own launch share
paragraphs: Launch result report of {set:company}, dated {today}. Title: {col:launchres.title}. Release date: {col:launchres.release_date}.

Copies in the first 7 days: {col:launchres.copies_7d}. In the first 30 days: {col:launchres.copies_30d}. In the first 12 months: {col:launchres.copies_12m}. Royalties in the first 30 days: {col:launchres.royalties_30d}.
Launch share (the share of the first 12 months sold in the first 30 days): {col:launchres.launch_share}. Your own average: {col:launchres.own_avg}. Verdict: {col:launchres.verdict}.
Pre-orders at release: {col:launchres.pre_total}. Figures are estimates until the stores pay.

documents.title: Newsletter list growth report
paragraphs: List growth report of {set:company}, dated {today}. Month: {col:growth.month}.

Sends: {col:growth.sends}. New subscribers: {col:growth.new}. Lost subscribers: {col:growth.lost}. Net growth: {col:growth.net}. List size at month end: {col:growth.list_size}. Growth: {col:growth.growth_pct}.
Open rate: {col:growth.open_rate}. Click rate: {col:growth.click_rate}. Royalties in 7 days from the sends: {col:growth.royalties_7d}.
Compare with the same month a year ago on the List Growth by Month sheet.

documents.title: Reviewer list summary for one reviewer
paragraphs: Reviewer summary of {set:company}, dated {today}. Reviewer: {col:ranking.name} ({col:ranking.kind}), phone {col:ranking.phone}.

Copies sent: {col:ranking.copies_sent}. Reviews posted: {col:ranking.reviews_posted}. Response rate: {col:ranking.response_rate}. Average days to a review: {col:ranking.avg_days}. Rank on the list: {col:ranking.rank}.
Verdict against your own targets: {col:ranking.verdict}. A reviewer with few copies is tested before you decide.
Write your decision below.
